dedupe_keys.name: residents planned behaviour of waste sorting gama agent based model of source separation of municipal waste in urban areas

description: This agent-based model, built on the GAMA platform by Jonathan Edgardo Cohen, explores what drives residents to sort their household waste properly at source. It applies the Theory of Planned Behaviour, in which attitudes, social norms and perceived control shape intentions, to residents in urban situations, because the success of source separation, adopted by many cities to raise recycling and cut greenhouse gas emissions, depends on citizen behaviour. The associated paper appeared in Waste Management (doi 10.1016/j.wasman.2024.12.020). Version 1.4.0, released in March 2024, is available as a free download from the CoMSES library under a CC-BY-4.0 licence and runs in the free GAMA platform. Caveats: behaviour parameters come from the study's own setting, the library page does not give the city, and collection logistics are not the focus. Coverage is general urban municipal waste. Simulation uses: estimating separated waste streams for collection and treatment planning under different information or incentive policies. Related records: the What a Waste global database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) gives city and country waste generation baselines.
inputs: Urban area with households and waste containers
Theory of Planned Behaviour parameters (attitudes, norms, perceived control)
